title: "Thank you Miss Rosa" By Allen St.  Pierre. One Brave Person Can Make The Crucial Difference.

content_html_sanitized:
The Parks saw that only a principled stand against racist Jim Crow laws coupled with their self-sacrifice, compounded with the self-sacrificing of tens of thousands of other similarly situated African Americans, could lead to a tipping point in the civil rights movement.
 
Blessedly, they were right.
 
Like the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) before it, since 1970, NORML has been the catalyst for stakeholders and cannabis consumers to get organized, lobby and litigate for equal rights for citizens who choose to consume cannabis.  Due to NORMLs long-standing reform efforts and support from the general public who use cannabis, there are now tens of thousands of cannabis reform activists whove attended NORML conferences, seminars and rallies.
 
Decades old government policies against cannabis doggedly remain in place, yet now, thousands of concerned citizens are trained and the publics dissonance in favor of serious cannabis law reform is growing larger everyday.
 
I often wonder to myself who will be the next Rosa Parks?
 
Last night before I retired to bed I broke out one of my all time favorite compilations of American music, from a great American band, The Neville Brothers Yellow Moon.
 
Since the late 1980s whenever I hear the name Rosa Parks, in my head, I almost always hear the introduction of the Nevilles Sister Rosa.*
 
From everyone at NORML, thank you Mrs. Rosa Parks, for all your strength, courage and for being such a potent symbol of what an individual and self-sacrificing act can accomplish towards a larger and higher goal.
 
Ever higher,
 
Allen St. Pierre
Executive Director
Member, Board of Directors
NORML/NORML Foundation
 director@norml.org
